notes: Statements from the Q2 complaint log plus three short interviews at pickup (June 24-25). The tree lands on a binary CTQ: an order either survives its first presentation or it does not -- there is no partial credit in the customer's test, which is what makes this the attribute thread (pass/fail units, proportions math) rather than a measured quantity.

customers.role: internal -- faculty ordering course packets and exam sets
internal -- department admin staff ordering programs, posters, signage
external -- student organizations at the retail counter

statements.text: The course packets came back with the chapter dividers trimmed crooked -- I sent the whole box back.
statements.source_detail: Q2 log #23, June -- the 90-packet order returned in one box

statements.text: The flyers were on flimsy paper, not the cardstock I picked on the form.
I ordered 250 programs and the box had 210, the afternoon of the event.
There were smudge streaks across the first twenty pages of the exam copies.
I don't have time to proof your work at the counter -- it needs to be right the first time I see it.

needs.text: The order is right the first time it is presented -- the customer never has to inspect, return, or wait for a redo.
What was ordered is what is delivered -- the specified stock and the exact quantity.
Print and finish quality is clean enough to hand out as-is -- straight trim, no visible smudge or banding.

ctqs.measure: First-presentation acceptance, binary per order: the order passes all four named checks at the QC desk -- paper stock matches the ticket, trim within 2 mm of spec, no smudge or banding visible at arm's length, quantity exact. Tracked as the proportion of orders REJECTED (defect rate), daily, by shift.
ctqs.critical_vs_easy_check: The easy number is turnaround time -- the order system already stamps it. The statements point somewhere else: S5 is a right-first-time demand, S1-S4 are four concrete ways an order fails it. Pass/fail at first presentation is the customer's own test, and it is measurable at the QC desk in under a minute with the four named checks.

ctqs.measure: Turnaround: business days from order confirmation to ready-for-pickup
ctqs.target: hold at or under the Q2 median (1.9 days) while the defect work runs
ctqs.critical_vs_easy_check: Turnaround IS the easy-to-measure number -- kept, but demoted: it rides as the charter's first consequential metric so the defect fix cannot quietly buy quality with speed, not as a second primary.

charter_metric_link: C1 is the charter's primary metric verbatim: first-presentation defect rate, proportion of orders (0-1), baseline 0.086, target 0.043 by 2026-09-30. C2 is the charter's consequential metric 'median turnaround (business days)' -- a guardrail, not a second goal.
